newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Ogoni group alleges new arrests by Nigerian force.
newsitem.headline: Ogoni group alleges new arrests by Nigerian force.

text.p: The minority rights group of hanged activist Ken Saro-Wiwa said on Friday that several Ogoni kinsmen including a former senator had been arrested in a new crackdown in the volatile oil-producing area of southeastern Nigeria.

But the military officer in charge of security in the area denied the allegation. "Neither Senator Cyrus Gbene-Nunieh nor any other Ogoni person has been arrested," said Major Obi Umahi by telephone from the area.

The Movement for the Survival of Ogoni Peoples (MOSOP) group, which Saro-Wiwa led before his execution last November, said in a statement that the elderly Gbene-Nunieh and five Ogonis were arrested on Wednesday while holding a meeting in the town hall by a security team led by Umahi.
"All those arrested including Cyrus Gbene-Nunieh are being held incommunicado and denied access to their families and personal physicians," said MOSOP.
But Umahi countered that the former senator was in his home.

"What happened is that he convened a peace meeting which is what government wants but he did not obtain clearance as required," he said, adding "I spoke to him as a son to a father and he apologised. That's all."
Nigeria caused international outrage last November when then MOSOP president Saro-Wiwa president and eight other MOSOP activists were hanged for the murder of four Ogoni chiefs.
They had been tried under a military decree condemned worldwide as unfair. Nigeria was suspended from the Commonwealth and various sanctions imposed on it by mainly Western nations.
In April, a United Nations fact-finding mission visited Nigeria and recommended changes to the nation's draconian laws and compensation for the families of the Ogoni activists.
Nigeria changed the laws but said no compensations would be paid.
Umahi said the MOSOP statement was aimed at drawing attention to it in the runup to the anniversary of the hanging.
"There is no tension in Ogoniland," he said, adding "The state governor was here today to comission a new hospital in Gokana town and there is still merriment going on now."

MOSOP campaigns for self-determination for the 500,000 Ogonis in the Niger Delta and has also been seeking compensation from Anglo-Dutch oil giant Shell for alleged ecological damage to the area from its oil activities there.
